title: Two coverings of an object have a common refinement
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] and let $\mathcal U=\{U_i\to U\}_{i\in I}$ and $\mathcal V=\{V_j\to U\}_{j\in J}$ be coverings of the same object $U$. Then $\mathcal W=\{V_j\times_UU_i\to U\}_{(i,j)\in I\times J}$ (any choice of the fibre products, which exist by axiom (iii)) is a covering of $U$, and the projections $V_j\times_UU_i\to U_i$, $V_j\times_UU_i\to V_j$ with the index maps $(i,j)\mapsto i$, $(i,j)\mapsto j$ are morphisms of coverings $\mathcal W\to\mathcal U$ and $\mathcal W\to\mathcal V$ over $\mathrm{id}_U$ [def-weil-pbc-site-plus-construction] (b). In particular any finitely many coverings of $U$ have a common refinement.

proof.text: *Pull back the second covering along each member of the first.* For every $i\in I$, apply axiom (iii) of the site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] to the covering $\{V_j\to U\}_{j\in J}$ and the morphism $U_i\to U$. Choose the resulting fibre products $W_{ij}=V_j\times_UU_i$ with projections $q_{ij}:W_{ij}\to U_i$ and $p_{ij}:W_{ij}\to V_j$. For each fixed $i$, the family $\{q_{ij}:W_{ij}\to U_i\}_{j\in J}$ is a covering.

source.place: Sites, Lemma 00W6 and proof: the first sentence, applying the base-change axiom to \{V_j\to U\} along each U_i\to U

proof.text: *Compose the pulled-back coverings.* Apply axiom (ii) of [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] to the covering $\{U_i\to U\}_{i\in I}$ and the covering $\{q_{ij}:W_{ij}\to U_i\}_{j\in J}$ for each $i$. The family $\{W_{ij}\to U\}_{(i,j)\in I\times J}$, whose maps are the composites $W_{ij}\xrightarrow{q_{ij}}U_i\to U$, is therefore a covering of $U$.

source.place: Sites, Lemma 00W6 and proof: the second sentence, applying the composition axiom to the pulled-back families

proof.text: *Refinement maps.* The projection $q_{ij}:W_{ij}\to U_i$ together with the index map $(i,j)\mapsto i$ is a morphism of coverings from $\mathcal W$ to $\mathcal U$ over $\mathrm{id}_U$, because $(U_i\to U)\circ q_{ij}$ is the structure map of $W_{ij}$. Likewise $p_{ij}:W_{ij}\to V_j$ and $(i,j)\mapsto j$ define a morphism from $\mathcal W$ to $\mathcal V$ over $\mathrm{id}_U$. These are precisely the canonical projections of the fibre products, so $\mathcal W$ is a common refinement.

source.place: Sites, Lemma 00W6 (00W6) and the definition of morphism of coverings in Definition 00VT

proof.text: *Finitely many coverings.* Iterating the binary construction gives a common refinement for any finite list of coverings: refine the first two, then refine the result with the third, and so on. The induction uses only the just-proved binary case and the transitivity of morphisms of coverings [def-weil-pbc-site-plus-construction] (b).

source.place: Sites, Lemma 00W6; finite-family assertion is the immediate finite induction on the binary common-refinement construction

lean.statement: theorem siteCoverings_common_refinement {C : Type u} [SmallCategory C] (J : Precoverage C) [J.HasIsos] [J.IsStableUnderComposition] [J.IsStableUnderBaseChange] [J.HasPullbacks] {U : C} (E : ZeroHypercover.{w} J U) (F : ZeroHypercover.{w'} J U) (W : E.I₀ × F.I₀ → C) (q : ∀ ij : E.I₀ × F.I₀, W ij ⟶ E.X ij.1) (p : ∀ ij : E.I₀ × F.I₀, W ij ⟶ F.X ij.2) (h : ∀ ij : E.I₀ × F.I₀, IsPullback (p ij) (q ij) (F.f ij.2) (E.f ij.1)) : Presieve.ofArrows W (fun ij => q ij ≫ E.f ij.1) ∈ J U ∧ (∃ r : PreZeroHypercover.Hom { I₀ := E.I₀ × F.I₀, X := W, f := fun ij => q ij ≫ E.f ij.1 } E.toPreZeroHypercover, r.s₀ = _root_.Prod.fst ∧ HEq r.h₀ q) ∧ (∃ r : PreZeroHypercover.Hom { I₀ := E.I₀ × F.I₀, X := W, f := fun ij => q ij ≫ E.f ij.1 } F.toPreZeroHypercover, r.s₀ = _root_.Prod.snd ∧ HEq r.h₀ p)
lean.note: The module also states the finite-family conclusion as siteCoverings_finite_common_refinement. The binary clause quantifies over arbitrary fibre products via IsPullback, rather than fixing Mathlib’s chosen pullbacks.
